key_insight: Sensor2Sensor learns to convert in-the-wild, single-sensor video (e.g., dashcams) into the sensor modalities used by AV fleets, enabling large-scale use of diverse, real-world data for ADS training and validation.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between limited, proprietary AV sensor datasets and vast, diverse but unstructured in-the-wild video by generating target AV sensor modalities from different embodiments and setups.
method: Train a cross-embodiment conversion model that maps source in-the-wild sensor streams to target AV sensor modalities (e.g., surround cameras, lidar-like representations) while accounting for different camera placements and vehicle geometry.

Leverage geometry- and semantics-aware learning with a mix of paired, weakly-supervised, and domain-adaptive objectives to preserve spatial layout, object identity, and dynamic behaviors across conversions.
Produce realistic, target-modality outputs suitable for downstream ADS tasks (perception, tracking, validation) so they can be used to augment training and offline evaluation.
impact: Enables practitioners to massively expand and diversify ADS training and validation data using readily available dashcam and in-the-wild video, reducing dependence on costly AV fleet collection and improving coverage of long-tail scenarios.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing source in-the-wild dashcam input, cross-embodiment conversion model, and generated AV sensor outputs (surround cameras, depth/lidar proxies).

Bar chart or table comparing dataset scale/diversity and downstream model performance with and without Sensor2Sensor augmentation.

paper_title: Sensor2Sensor: Cross-Embodiment Sensor Conversion for Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Jiahao Wang, Bo Sun, Yijing Bai, Vincent Casser, Songyou Peng
